YOUR INFORMATION MATTERS

Privacy policy

How information is handled when you discover suppliers, organise a wedding, run a supplier business and make payments through WedSparks.

Prepared for review · 18 October 2026 · Not yet effective. Business identity, contact details and operational rules require confirmation.

1. About this policy2. Information you provide3. Guest information and sensitive details4. Technical information and local storage5. Why information is used6. What suppliers and other users can see7. 1. About this policy

This policy describes the proposed handling of personal information by the operator of WedSparks. It covers visitors, couple accounts, supplier accounts, invited guests and people who contact us. Public supplier information and private wedding planning information have different audiences. This policy should be read with the Platform Terms, Credit Programme Terms and any notice shown when information is collected.

Review draft dated 18 October 2026. Before this becomes effective, the operating legal entity, business address, privacy contact, relevant service providers and overseas processing locations must be inserted and verified. References to payment and subscription services describe the intended launch service and must be checked against the deployed implementation.

2. Information you provide

Account information may include your name, email address, authentication details and account preferences. Couples may provide a partner’s name, wedding date, location, guest count, budget, tasks, supplier preferences and booking information. Suppliers may provide business and contact details, service areas, availability, packages, photographs, descriptions, policies and information needed to verify or administer their business account.

We also process information you choose to include in enquiries, conversations, quotes, invoices, reviews, support requests and wedding submissions. Please avoid including identity documents, full payment card details or other unnecessary sensitive information in messages or uploads. A public business profile can still contain personal information, especially for sole traders.

3. Guest information and sensitive details

Guest lists and RSVP responses can include names, attendance, contact details and dietary or accessibility requirements. Some of these details may reveal health, religious or other sensitive information. Provide only what is needed to organise the wedding, explain the intended use to guests, and obtain any permission required before sharing another person’s information.

Invitation links should be sent privately to their intended recipients. A person who receives a link may be able to access the information made available through that invitation. Share catering or accessibility information only with people who need it, rather than publishing a full guest list or sensitive individual requirements. Guest participation is not permission to add someone to marketing lists.

4. Technical information and local storage

Operating a website can involve processing IP addresses, browser and device information, request times, error records and security logs. We use information necessary to deliver pages, maintain sessions, investigate faults and protect accounts. Public tool preferences, such as checklist ticks, may be stored in your browser and can be removed through browser settings.

The final cookie and storage inventory must identify the technologies actually deployed, their purposes, providers and retention. Optional advertising or analytics technologies must be disclosed before use and appropriate consent controls supplied where required. This draft does not assert that advertising trackers, cross-site profiling or a particular analytics product are currently used.

5. Why information is used

Information is used to provide accounts and planning tools; display published supplier storefronts; deliver enquiries and conversations; manage invitations and replies; organise booking and payment records; calculate and administer credits; handle account support; and investigate misuse or disputes. Relevant information may also be used to improve reliability and understand which features need improvement.

Where consent is the basis for a particular optional activity, declining it should not prevent unrelated core functions. We will not treat creating a private wedding account as consent to publish it as a supplier lead. Information collected for a specific wedding task should not be reused for an unrelated purpose without a valid basis and any required notice or permission.

6. What suppliers and other users can see

Published storefront content is intended to be visible to the public and may be indexed by search engines or cited by third-party discovery services. Information you send to a supplier becomes available to that supplier and relevant authorised account users. Suppliers may keep records necessary for their own service obligations and must explain their own privacy practices.

Private planning records are not intended to be public directory content. Before sharing a quote request, check the wedding details included in it. When you upload photographs or other material, ensure you have the right to share it and permission from identifiable people where needed. Search engine copies may take time to disappear after public content is removed.

7. Optional Couple Leads

Couple Leads is intended to let subscribed suppliers discover relevant couples who have actively chosen to hear from businesses. The opt-in screen must explain which wedding details are visible, the intended suppliers and how to switch discovery off. Only information reasonably needed for that introduction should be displayed; private guest lists, full addresses and financial records should not be exposed.

Suppliers must use lead information only for relevant wedding enquiries and respect requests to stop contact. Access is not permission to export, resell or build unrelated marketing databases. Turning discovery off prevents future discovery through the feature; it cannot erase information already lawfully received by a supplier, whose own retention responsibilities also apply.

8. Payment and credit information

Payment services require transaction information, such as invoice references, amounts, currency, payment status, refunds and processor identifiers. Credits require a record of qualifying money paid, milestones earned, credits used and adjustments. Payment providers may collect additional billing, fraud prevention, identity or supplier payout information directly under their own notices.

Do not send payment card numbers or bank credentials through chat. Before launch, the final notice must identify the payment provider, distinguish information collected directly by that provider from information WedSparks receives, and verify any statements about card storage or payment security. WedSparks does not describe ordinary payment processing as escrow, a trust account or insurance.

9. Service providers and overseas processing

Information may be handled by providers supplying hosting, authentication, database storage, email delivery, payment processing, customer support or security services. They should receive only what is necessary for the service they perform and be subject to appropriate contractual and access controls. Relevant information may also be disclosed to professional advisers or authorities when there is a lawful need.

Some providers may process information outside your country. Before publication, confirm the actual providers, hosting regions, likely overseas recipients and the safeguards applicable to those transfers. Do not assume a provider’s global operations mean that every location receives your information. No sale of private couple or guest information is authorised by this draft.

10. Communications and marketing

Service communications can include verification, account security, conversation alerts, booking updates, payment reminders and information about your credits. Optional promotional communications should have an appropriate permission basis and a clear way to unsubscribe. Unsubscribing from marketing does not necessarily stop essential account or transaction messages.

A supplier receiving an enquiry must not assume the couple has subscribed to the supplier’s wider marketing programme. If you receive an unexpected message or suspect misuse of a lead, retain the relevant details and raise the concern through the published support route once configured.

11. Security and retention

Access should be limited according to account roles and the purpose of the feature. Keep your own credentials private, use a strong unique password and check that an invitation or business link is intended for the recipient. No online system can promise absolute security; suspected account compromise should be reported promptly.

Information should be kept only as long as reasonably needed for the relevant purpose, legal recordkeeping, fraud prevention or an unresolved dispute. Deleting an account may not immediately remove transaction records, necessary audit information or backups. The final retention schedule must define the actual periods and deletion arrangements rather than promise an unimplemented automatic deadline.

12. Access, correction and other requests

You may be able to view or correct information in your account. For information you cannot change yourself, request access, correction or deletion through the privacy contact to be published before launch. We may need proportionate identity checks and information that helps locate the relevant record. If a request cannot be fulfilled, we should explain why and any available review route.

Rights depend on the law that applies and may include complaint, access, correction or deletion rights. Records held independently by a supplier or payment provider may need to be requested from that organisation. We will not require payment or unnecessary identity information merely to receive a privacy complaint.

13. Children, third-party links and public stories

Account holders should be adults capable of entering the relevant agreement. Guest planning may include children’s names and requirements; an organising adult should share only necessary information and obtain appropriate parental or guardian permission. Children’s photographs should not be published merely because they appear in a wedding submission.

External websites have their own practices. Importing your own business text does not authorise access to a competitor account, and we do not ask for competitor passwords. Real wedding stories require publication permissions and image credits; sensitive private planning information should not be included in the published story.

14. Complaints and changes

Raise a privacy concern with the WedSparks privacy contact, describing the information, event and outcome you seek. We should investigate, explain our response and identify further complaint options under applicable law, including the Australian Information Commissioner or New Zealand Privacy Commissioner where relevant.

Material changes to purposes or sharing should be explained before they take effect where required. The final policy must show its effective date and an accessible contact route. This review draft is not a substitute for verifying the actual platform configuration and applicable privacy obligations.
